name: Documents

hero.title: Write the report once. Send it as a PDF, a spreadsheet or a Slack message.
hero.lede: Build invoices, reports and notifications from JSX, then render the same tree to any of 20 formats, from PDF and Word to Teams cards and Notion blocks. Text formats need nothing else; PDF, Word, Excel and PowerPoint use an engine you install only if you emit them.

why.title: One template instead of one per format.

items.title: Twenty outputs, one tree
items.text: The same invoice becomes a PDF attachment, an email body, a Markdown file and a Slack message. Change a heading once. Your own components work inside the tree.

items.title: Install only what you emit
items.text: pdfmake, docx, exceljs and pptxgenjs are optional peers, imported the first time you render that format. An app that only sends email never installs them, and a missing one fails with the exact `bun add` command.

items.title: User text stays text
items.text: Link and image URLs go through an allowlist, CSV cells starting with `=`, `+`, `-` or `@` are neutralised, Markdown text is escaped, and a Slack link cannot smuggle in `<!channel>`.

items.title: Every channel speaks its own format
items.text: Slack gets Block Kit, Teams an Adaptive Card, Notion blocks, Confluence and Jira ADF, Telegram HTML, email a 600px table layout with Outlook-safe buttons.

difference.title: Three formats used to mean three templates.

before.label: pdfmake + hand-built Slack + CSV
before.caption: Each format has its own shape, so one report is three templates to keep in step. The CSV breaks on a value like `$1,000` and passes `=HYPERLINK(…)` straight to Excel.

after.label: with @pyreon/document
after.caption: One component. Pick the format at the call site.
after.code:
import { Document, Page, Heading, Text, Table, render } from '@pyreon/document'

const rows: [string, string][] = [['US', '$1M'], ['EU', '$800K']]
const Report = (props: { rows: [string, string][] }) => (
  <Document title="Q4 Report">
    <Page>
      <Heading>Sales report</Heading>
      <Text>Q4 2026 performance summary.</Text>
      <Table columns={['Region', 'Revenue']} rows={props.rows} />
    </Page>
  </Document>
)
const report = <Report rows={rows} />

await render(report, 'pdf')    // Uint8Array (with pdfmake installed)
await render(report, 'slack')  // Block Kit JSON
await render(report, 'csv')    // quoted, formula-safe
await render(report, 'email')  // table layout, Outlook-safe buttons

comingFrom.title: A document definition becomes components
comingFrom.before:
import pdfMake from 'pdfmake/build/pdfmake'
import pdfFonts from 'pdfmake/build/vfs_fonts'
import type { TDocumentDefinitions } from 'pdfmake/interfaces'

pdfMake.addVirtualFileSystem(pdfFonts) // Roboto, the default font, as base64

const rows = [['US', '$1M'], ['EU', '$800K']]

const pdf: TDocumentDefinitions = {
  info: { title: 'Q4 Report' },
  content: [
    { text: 'Sales report', style: 'header' },
    'Q4 2026 performance summary.',
    { table: { headerRows: 1, body: [['Region', 'Revenue'], ...rows] } },
  ],
  styles: { header: { fontSize: 22, bold: true } },
}

pdfMake.createPdf(pdf).download('q4.pdf')
comingFrom.after:
import { Document, Page, Heading, Text, Table, download } from '@pyreon/document'

const rows: [string, string][] = [['US', '$1M'], ['EU', '$800K']]

await download(
  <Document title="Q4 Report">
    <Page>
      <Heading>Sales report</Heading>
      <Text>Q4 2026 performance summary.</Text>
      <Table columns={['Region', 'Revenue']} rows={rows} />
    </Page>
  </Document>,
  'q4.pdf',
)
comingFrom.note: pdfmake still draws the PDF: keep it installed. The extension on the file name picks the format, so `q4.docx` or `q4.md` works the same way.

limits.title: Binary formats need their engine
limits.text: Install `pdfmake`, `docx`, `exceljs` or `pptxgenjs` for PDF, DOCX, XLSX or PPTX. They load on first use; render on the server if you would rather not ship them to browsers.

limits.title: A render is a snapshot
limits.text: Signals in the tree are read once. Render again to pick up new values.

limits.title: Table cells are plain values
limits.text: Each cell is a string or a number. Put rich content in the blocks around the table.

limits.title: Formats differ in what they can show
limits.text: Slack shows a table as a code block, WhatsApp as pipe-separated lines, and chat formats turn a page break into a divider; each renderer does the closest thing its platform has. Check a chat payload in the platform's preview before you rely on it.

limits.title: Web and server only
limits.text: Rendering runs in browsers, Node and Bun, not inside iOS or Android apps. Build the file on a server and fetch it, or hand it to the share sheet.

recipes.text: The `slack` output is a Block Kit payload an incoming webhook accepts as is.

faq.q: Do I pay for pdfmake if I only send email?
faq.a: No. The four binary engines are optional peer dependencies and are imported only when you render their format. If you never render a PDF, pdfmake is never installed or bundled.

faq.q: Is it safe to render user content?
faq.a: That is the default. URLs are allowlisted (links: `http`, `https`, `mailto`, `tel` and relative; images: `http`, `https`, relative and `data:image`), a rejected link renders as its label, CSV cells are guarded against formula injection, and Markdown, Discord and Slack text is escaped.

faq.q: Can I use my own components?
faq.a: Yes. Any component that returns document primitives can sit in the tree; `render()` resolves it first. A DOM element such as `<div>` throws with a message naming it, because a PDF has no idea what a div is.

faq.q: Can I add a format we need?
faq.a: Register a renderer with `registerRenderer('thermal', { render(node) { … } })` and call `render(doc, 'thermal')`. It receives the same `DocNode` tree the built-in renderers get.

faq.q: Does it run in a native app?
faq.a: Not on the device. Render on your server and fetch the file, or hand it to the system share sheet; both of those lower to iOS and Android on the experimental native targets.

end.title: One report. Every format someone will ask for next week.
